description: Orchestrate sandboxed coding agents in TypeScript with sandcastle.run()

latest_release.name: v0.14.0
latest_release.body:
### Minor Changes

- d99fff8: Add an E2B isolated sandbox provider, `e2b()` from `@ai-hero/sandcastle/sandboxes/e2b`. It needs the optional `e2b` peer dependency and `E2B_API_KEY` (or the `apiKey` option). Use a template that ships your agent's CLI, such as `e2b({ template: "claude" })`.
- 8783573: Add `modal()`, an isolated sandbox provider for [Modal](https://modal.com) sandboxes, at `@ai-hero/sandcastle/sandboxes/modal`. Install `modal` (an optional peer dependency) and set `MODAL_TOKEN_ID` and `MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET`, or pass `tokenId` and `tokenSecret`. By default it builds a `node:24-bookworm` image with Claude Code installed; pass `image` for your own. Sandboxes live for an hour unless `timeoutMs` says otherwise, and `sandboxId` is the Modal sandbox id.
- 775a8df: Add `sprites()`, a Fly.io Sprites isolated sandbox provider, at `@ai-hero/sandcastle/sandboxes/sprites`. It needs `@fly/sprites` (an optional peer dependency, which asks for Node 24 or later) and a token in `SPRITES_TOKEN` (or `SPRITE_TOKEN`, or the `token` option). Each sandbox is a new Sprite with the repo at `/home/sprite/workspace`; `sandboxId` is the Sprite's name. Sprites persist until deleted, so Sandcastle deletes the Sprite on `close()`, when setup fails, and from a background process when the run is interrupted or exits without closing it.

### Patch Changes

- 73ce215: docker() and podman(): the worktree admin directories can no longer be renamed from inside the sandbox.
- 14507d6: Add a Glossary page to the user docs (`docs/guide/glossary.md`, in the Reference group) that defines every term in one place. Guide pages no longer open with definition blocks; instead, each page links the first mention of a term to its glossary entry.

detail.readme: ## What is Sandcastle? A TypeScript library for orchestrating AI coding agents in isolated sandboxes: 1. You invoke agents with a single `sandcastle.run()`. 2. Sandcastle handles sandboxing the agent with a configurable branch strategy. 3. The commits made on the branches get merged back. Sandcastle is provider-agnostic. It ships with native sandboxes that use your OS's own process sandbox (Bubblewrap on Linux and WSL2, Seatbelt on macOS), image-based providers for Docker and Podman, and cloud providers for Daytona, E2B, Fly.io Sprites, Modal and Vercel, and you can create your own. Great for parallelizing multiple AFK agents, creating review pipelines, or even just orchestrating your own agents. ## Documentation The docs live in [`docs/guide`](./docs/guide), one page per major term, with every term defined in the [Glossary](./docs/guide/glossary.md), and are published at [aihero.dev/sandcastle](https://www.aihero.dev/sandcastle). - [Getting started](./docs/guide/getting-started.md): prerequisites and a quick start - Core: [Core concepts](./docs/guide/core-concepts.md) - Sandboxes: [Sandbox providers](./docs/guide/sandbox-providers.md) - Branching: [Branch strategies](./docs/guide/branch-strategies.md) - Agents: [Agent providers](./docs/guide/agent-providers.md), [Agent sessions](./docs/guide/agent-sessions.md) - Execution: [Iterations](./docs/guide/iterations.md), [Structured output](./docs/guide/structured-output.md) - Prompts: [Prompts](./docs/guide/prompts.md) - Hooks: [Hooks](./docs/guide/hooks.md) - Init: [Init](./docs/guide/init.md) - Display: [Run logs](./docs/guide/run-logs.md) - Reference: [`run()` and `createSandbox()`](./docs/guide/run.md), [CLI commands](./docs/guide/cli.md), [Glossary](./docs/guide/glossary.md) ## Development ```bash npm install npm run build # Bundle with tsup npm test # Run tests with vitest npm run typecheck # Type-check ``` ## License MIT
